content:
This honestly is mostly a question for @Sofia Rodrigues but anyone can answer I guess.
I’ve been watching closely the development of the Async/HTTP stuff. As someone whose familiar with Async stuff in Rust, I’ve run into problems with deadlocks and other concurrency related bugs, so I’m curious if there’s a way to formally verify programs that use STD.Async to prevent deadlocks.

All of the concurrency infrastructure is built on top of IO, so verification infrastructure for Async would be part of a larger push to enable some form of verification for IO programs. This is something the FRO wants to look into, but it is in the "if all goes well we might get to it in five years" category.

I know that a foundation to typecheck against deadlocks is using quatitative dependent types (like idris 2), and especially linear types.
I dont know if that's possible to add to Lean as i heard from leo interview that changing the type theory of lean is out of scope.
Maybe i'st possible as a front-end compiler feature only not enforced by the kernel.
Because i think writing proofs about this will be tedious vs having it just typecheck natively or simulation of a typecheck likewhat has been done for coinductive types

One option, if you're interested in verifying against protocol-level issues such as deadlocks, is to verify a model of your concurrent system, and then trust an embedding of that model into IO to execute it. This may allow you to gain confidence about your code without solving the much harder problem of IO verification.
